title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. For the first face, draw a circle with its center at coordinates (0.0097, 0.0097) and a radius of 0.0097 units. Inside this circle, draw a second, smaller concentric circle with the same center point but a radius of 0.0085 units. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.0194 to achieve the desired dimensions. Since the Euler angles and translation vector are already set to zero, no further transformation is necessary. Extrude the scaled sketch 0.75 units along the positive normal direction without extending it in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The resulting cylindrical object will have a length and width of 0.01935483870967742 units and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the cylindrical section
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0097, 0.0097)  # Move to the center of the circles
    .circle(0.0097)  # Outer circle
    .circle(0.0085)  # Inner circle
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylindrical section
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Create the small rectangular section at the top
# Define the dimensions of the rectangle
rect_length = 0.01935483870967742
rect_width = 0.01935483870967742

# Create the rectangle sketch
rect_sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0097, 0.0097)  # Move to the center of the rectangle
    .rect(rect_length, rect_width)  # Create the rectangle
)

# Extrude the rectangle sketch to create the rectangular section
rect_extrusion = rect_sketch.extrude(0.01)  # Extrude by a small amount

# Combine the cylindrical section and the rectangular section
r = cylinder.union(rect_extrusion)

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the circular sketch
circle_center = (0.0097, 0.0097)
circle_radius = 0.0097
sketch = workplane.center(*circle_center).circle(circle_radius)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylindrical rod
extrude_depth = 0.75
cylinder = sketch.extrude(extrude_depth)

# Scale the sketch for the rectangular cross-section
sketch_scale = 0.0193
scaled_sketch = workplane.center(*circle_center).rect(sketch_scale, sketch_scale)

# Extrude the scaled sketch to create the rectangular cross-section
rect_extrude_depth = 0.01
rectangle = scaled_sketch.extrude(rect_extrude_depth)

# Combine the cylinder and the rectangle
r = cylinder.union(rectangle)

import cadquery as cq
import math

# Overall dimensions
total_height = 0.75
hex_across_corners = 0.0194
hex_circumradius = hex_across_corners / 2.0
hex_height = 0.020
shaft_diameter = 0.0170
shaft_radius = shaft_diameter / 2.0

# Hex nut section at the bottom
hex_nut = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .polygon(6, 2 * hex_circumradius)
    .extrude(hex_height)
)

# Cylindrical shaft running the full height
shaft = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .circle(shaft_radius)
    .extrude(total_height)
)

# Combine into one solid
r = shaft.union(hex_nut)

import cadquery as cq

# Base square rod, 0.0194 x 0.0194 cross-section, 0.75 tall
r = cq.Workplane("XY").box(0.0194, 0.0194, 0.75, centered=(True, True, False))

# Round the top end edges (rounded rim seen in isometric/top views)
r = r.faces(">Z").edges().fillet(0.002)

# Chamfer the bottom end edges (beveled base seen in isometric view)
r = r.faces("<Z").edges().chamfer(0.0015)

# Central through hole along the Z axis
r = r.faces(">Z").workplane().hole(0.0097)
